name: University of Connecticut
description:
The University of Connecticut is a public land-grant research university in Storrs, Connecticut. It was founded in 1881 as the Storrs Agricultural School and has since grown to prepare students for a starting salary of $46,400 in fields such as economics and communication.

Over 3,400 international students from more than 113 countries enroll at the University annually and join one of the 40+ international student associations.

State-of-the-art classrooms, research labs, and libraries are all part of the first-rate academic facilities the University of Connecticut offers. Athletic facilities are a big part of campus life. The Werth Family UConn Basketball Champions Center, the Sherman Family Sports Complex, and the Burton Family Football Complex are all accessible to students. The University invests in its facilities for students. The Student Recreation Center and outdoor fields are other ways students get their sporty fix and stay engaged with University life. The Student Union is a fun area with a movie theatre, game room, TV lounges, and a food court.

Student Life

A campus with over 700 student clubs is where students are engaged in student life and bringing everyone together. A community spirit is prevalent, as 1.3 million hours of community service are contributed annually. Six cultural centers can be found across campus that celebrate diversity. Eateries and restaurants line the campus for students to find places to satiate their hunger easily.

highlights.title: Accommodation
highlights.value: There is a range of accommodation options at the University of Connecticut. International students find it easy to locate suitable accommodation on campus in dormitory rooms and apartments. First-year students must live on campus in residence halls to ingratiate themselves with the campus culture and quickly get to class. Research shows students who live on campus feel more connected to the university experience and perform better academically. On campus accommodation comes with communal kitchens, lounges, and laundry facilities. Students in higher years can choose between university apartments or suites as these arrangements offer more independent living arrangements. Special living accommodations for students with disabilities are also available.
